questions.question: If an array is declared as `arr[]={1,2,5,7,9};`, what is the value of `sizeof(arr[3])`?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) 2.** The paper assumes a 2-byte `int`; on a modern 32/64-bit compiler `sizeof(int)` is usually 4.
questions.sourceNote: Model answer follows the paper's 16-bit `int` assumption.

questions.question: ASCII code for `a`–`z` ranges from ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) 97–123.** Standard lowercase ASCII is 97–122; option C is the closest printed range, though its upper endpoint includes `{` at 123.
questions.sourceNote: The exact ASCII range is 97–122; option C is the intended printed choice.

questions.question: `s1="HI"`, `s2="HELLO"`, `s3="BYE"`. How can the three strings be concatenated?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) `strcat(s1,strcat(s2,s3))`.** `strcat` takes two arguments; the inner call appends `s3` to `s2`, then the result is appended to `s1`. A real program must also allocate enough writable space in `s1` and `s2`.

questions.question: A string is terminated by ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) `\0`.** The null character marks the end of a C string; the digit character `0` is not the terminator.

questions.question: The default storage class of a local variable is ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) auto.** Local variables are automatic by default.

questions.question: `*(&num)` is equivalent to writing ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) num.** Taking the address and dereferencing it cancels out.

questions.question: A structure placed within another structure is known as ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) nested structure.** A member whose type is another structure creates nesting.

questions.question: From which standard stream does a C program read data?
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) stdin.** `stdin` is the standard input stream; `stdout` and `stderr` are output streams.

questions.question: C is a ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: A) middle level language.** C combines high-level constructs with low-level memory access.

questions.question: If `a` is an integer variable, `a=5/2;` will return ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: C) 2.** Integer division truncates the fractional part.

questions.question: The `break` statement is used to exit from ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) a for loop.** `break` exits the nearest enclosing loop or `switch`; it does not exit an `if` by itself.

questions.question: A `do while` loop is useful when the statements within the loop must be executed ______.
questions.answer: **Correct answer: B) at least once.** Its condition is checked after the first iteration.

questions.question:
a) Distinguish between Structure and union.
b) Write a C program to insert `n` students’ data in a structure array named `Student` consisting of roll, name and marks of three subjects as member data. Display all those data and average marks of each student in tabular format.
questions.answer:
**a)** A structure allocates separate storage for every member, so all members can hold values simultaneously. A union overlays all members in one shared storage area, so only the last-written member is meaningful.

**b)** Define `struct Student { int roll; char name[50]; float marks[3]; };`, read `n`, loop over an array of `n` structures, compute `(marks[0]+marks[1]+marks[2])/3`, and print one aligned row per student. Use `%d`, `%s`, `%f` and a final average column; check `scanf` return values in production code.

subparts.text: Distinguish between Structure and union.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Write and display the student structure-array program with average marks.

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by parameter passing in C?
b) Explain different types of parameter passing supported by C using suitable examples.
questions.answer:
**a)** Parameter passing is the mechanism by which a caller supplies values or addresses to a function’s formal parameters.

**b)** C uses pass-by-value: copies of arguments are passed, so assignments to a parameter do not change the caller’s variable. Passing a pointer value emulates pass-by-reference because the function can dereference it to modify the original object, e.g. `void swap(int *a,int *b)`. Arrays decay to a pointer to their first element.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Define parameter passing in C.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Explain pass-by-value and pointer-based reference-like passing with examples.

questions.question:
a) What are the advantages of `switch`–`case` statements over nested `if`–`else` structure?
b) Write a C program to express any multiword string into its equivalent abbreviated form separated by a dot (`.`), i.e. `SWAPAN KUMAR SEN` will be written as `S.K.S.`.
questions.answer:
**a)** A `switch` is clearer and often compiles to a jump table when many discrete constant cases are tested; nested `if`–`else` chains are harder to read and evaluate conditions sequentially.

**b)** Print the first character of the input, then scan the remaining characters and whenever a space is followed by a non-space, print `.`, that character, and finally a trailing dot if the paper’s example format is required. Skip repeated spaces and preserve the rest of each word.

subparts.text: Advantages of switch-case over nested if-else.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Program to form a dot-separated abbreviation.

questions.question:
a) Create a two dimensional integer array to insert some integers randomly into it. Now find the greatest and smallest integer from the array and also find their corresponding locations.
b) What do you mean by pointer to a function? Give an example.
questions.answer:
**a)** Read row/column dimensions and elements, initialize `max=min=a[0][0]`, scan every `a[i][j]`, and update both values together with `(maxRow,maxCol)` and `(minRow,minCol)`.

**b)** A function pointer stores the address of a function and can call it indirectly. Example: `int (*op)(int,int) = add; int z = op(2,3);` where `int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}`.

questions.question:
a) What are the different kinds of modes available in C to open a file?
b) Write a program in C to create three different files `NUMBER`, `EVEN` and `ODD`. Insert some integer numbers randomly into `NUMBER`; from all those integers put all even numbers into `EVEN` and odd numbers into `ODD` respectively.
questions.answer:
**a)** Common text modes are `r`, `w`, `a`, `r+`, `w+`, `a+`; adding `b` selects binary mode (`rb`, `wb`, `ab`, `r+b`, etc.).

**b)** Open `NUMBER` for writing and store the integers; reopen it for reading and open `EVEN` and `ODD` for writing. For each `n`, write to `EVEN` when `n%2==0`, otherwise to `ODD`, and close all files.

subparts.text: List C file-opening modes.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Create NUMBER, EVEN and ODD and split integers by parity.

questions.question:
a) Write down at least three differences between entry controlled and exit controlled loop structures.
b) Write a C program to find all the prime numbers in a given range (upper and lower range should be given from the keyboard).
questions.answer:
**a)** Entry-controlled loops test the condition before the body (`for`, `while`); exit-controlled loops test after the body (`do while`). The body may execute zero times in an entry-controlled loop but at least once in an exit-controlled loop; the condition position and typical use cases also differ.

**b)** Read `lower` and `upper`, test each `n>=2` by trial division up to `sqrt(n)` or `i*i<=n`, and print `n` when no divisor is found. Handle `lower<2` by starting at 2.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: At least three differences between entry- and exit-controlled loops.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Program to print primes in a keyboard-supplied range.

questions.question:
a) Write a program in C to find the sum of the series `1+(1+2)+(1+2+3)+...` up to `n` terms; the value of `n` should be given from the keyboard.
b) Why should we avoid `goto` statement from our program?
questions.answer:
**a)** The k-th term is `k(k+1)/2`, so the sum is `n(n+1)(n+2)/6`. A loop can accumulate `inner += k; sum += inner;` for `k=1..n`.

**b)** Unrestricted jumps obscure control flow, make code harder to read, test and maintain, and can skip initialization/cleanup. Structured loops, functions and `break`/`continue` express the same logic more safely.

subparts.label: a
subparts.text: Program for the cumulative series sum up to n.

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Reasons to avoid goto.

questions.question:
a) What do you mean by pointer in C?
b) What are the advantages of pointer variable over memory variable?
c) Write a program in C to access the elements of a one dimensional array using pointer.
questions.answer:
**a)** A pointer is a variable that stores the address of another object of a declared type.

**b)** Pointers enable indirect access, efficient array/string traversal, dynamic memory, shared modification through function arguments, and linked data structures; they avoid copying large objects.

**c)** With `int a[5], *p=a;`, print `*(p+i)` for `i=0..4` (equivalently `p[i]`).

subparts.label: b
subparts.text: Advantages of pointer variables.

questions.question:
a) Write C programs to implement i) `strcpy()` and ii) `strlen()` library functions by yourself.
b) What do you mean by null character? Describe its uses in string manipulation.
questions.answer:
**a)** `my_strcpy(dest,src)` copies characters until the source `\0` and then writes the terminator; `my_strlen(s)` counts characters until `\0`. Both must assume valid, sufficiently large buffers.

**b)** The null character `\0` has numeric value zero and ends a C string. It lets standard functions detect length and termination, separates string data from unused buffer bytes, and is written by string-copy routines. It is different from the printable digit `'0'` and from a `NULL` pointer.
